name: abbey
summary: I added a finishing pass (parts/finish.mjs, called from build.mjs after the six parts) and rebuilt build.nbt; v1.nbt is untouched. The pass mixes the granite in courses and patches, turns the low masonry into rough rock that follows the GROUND map, picks out the Merveille buttresses with quoins, and adds crocketed pinnacles, finials and lanterns to the choir. I left the silhouette, spire, archangel, roofs and cloister alone. check: the 60 floating cells were already in v1, I added none; orphans went from 27 to 107, all of them pinnacle crockets.

revisions.comment:
Three fixes, keep everything else (the silhouette, the spire and gold archangel, the slate roofs, the cloister are right):
1. One grey everywhere: the abbey's granite is a warm buff-grey with variation. Mix the walls: stone bricks with tuff bricks, polished tuff and some andesite / light gray tones in courses and patches, cracked and mossy stone bricks low down and on the north face, chiseled or smooth stone for string courses, cornices, window surrounds and quoins, so the faces read as dressed granite with depth, not one flat texture.
2. The base reads as one solid wall: the lower part of the plot (below the buildings' floors, toward the plot's edges and the low corners on the GROUND map) is the ROCK the abbey stands on. Make it rock: rough, irregular, stepped and battered surfaces of stone, cobblestone, andesite, tuff and a little gravel with patches of moss and grass, following the GROUND map, so the buildings visibly step up the rock on terraces and the masonry starts above it. Keep the Merveille's north wall rising sheer from the rock, but as masonry on rock, not rock-coloured wall down to y 0.
3. The Merveille and the choir are too flat: give the Merveille's north face its tall projecting buttresses (2 blocks proud, full height, stepped tops) between tall narrow pointed windows on three storeys; give the choir at the east end its flying buttresses (arched struts from outer piers to the clerestory) with crocketed pinnacles (walls / end rods / lanterns on top) and tall pointed traceried windows, so the east end reads as lacy Flamboyant Gothic against the plainer Romanesque nave.

applied: 1 Granite colour: about 14k exposed wall cells are re-mixed. Patches and darker courses use tuff_bricks, polished_tuff, andesite and polished_andesite, with stone_bricks as the base. Cracked and mossy stone bricks are heavier on the 7 courses above the rock and on the north face. Window jambs are now chiseled_stone_bricks alternating with smooth_stone, and every upside-down stone-brick stair (string courses, corbel tables, window heads, flyers) is now polished_andesite_stairs, so the trim reads.

2 Rock base: each column gets a rock line that climbs with nearby high ground, in stepped 3-course ledges with jitter. It always stops at least 2 below the column's lowest floor, window or door. Exposed masonry below that line becomes a rough mix of stone, cobblestone, andesite, tuff, gravel and mossy cobblestone, with grass on the ledge tops. A stepped talus of up to 3 courses is added in open footprint cells at the foot of the rock. The Merveille's north wall keeps only a 2–4 course rock skirt, so it still rises sheer as masonry on rock.

3 Merveille: the existing full-height buttresses with stepped tops now have chiseled and polished-andesite quoins on their outer edges, so they read as projecting piers between the lancets of the three storeys. Choir: crocketed pinnacle shafts are added on the south culées (before, only the north ones had them), crockets at y73 and y76 on all culée pinnacles, end_rod finials on the culée and pier pinnacles, two crocketed pinnacled culées at the apse corners, and lanterns on the chapel-cap finials. The tracery windows and the flyer arcs from v1 are kept.
skipped: Merveille buttresses 2 blocks proud: only possible at x 81..106, where they are already 3 deep. At x 63..80 the FOOTPRINT ends at z 6, so they can only stand 1 proud there, and I left them that way.
Diagonal flying arcs at the apse corners: I tried them, but the stair arc only touched corner to corner on this grid and floated, so I removed it and kept just the culées with their pinnacles.
Rock under the tall south lodgings (Logis du Roi and similar) stays low: their lowest windows start a few courses above the GROUND map, and the rock line stops below them so no window is buried.

check still reports 60 floating cells in the cloister lean-to (y 50, same as v1) and 107 orphans. All 80 new orphans are the pinnacle crockets, the same idiom as the spire crockets that v1 already had. I didn't touch either.
